history.dynasty: None - a modern temple built through private philanthropy; managed by a charitable trust (Bitco/Bytco Charitable Trust per visitor guides)
history.period: 1971 (inauguration reported as 30 May 1971; one source says construction ran 1971-1973 - conflict, verify)
history.summary: Muktidham is a white-marble temple complex at Nashik Road, Nashik, built with white Makrana marble from Rajasthan by Rajasthani sculptors in a Nagara/Rajasthani style. It was founded in 1971 through the donation of the late J.D. Chauhan-Bytco, a local industrialist (also rendered Jairambhai/Jayram Bhai Bytco); the temple is privately operated through a trust. NOTE: the assignment brief named 'Udhavji Maharaj' as builder, but no published source supports that name - all sources credit J.D. Chauhan Bytco (verify). Its central idea is to let devotees visit replicas of all 12 Jyotirlingas under one roof - the replicas are built to the dimensions of the originals and were sanctified by being sent to their respective pilgrimage centres - so a darshan here is traditionally equated with visiting the Char Dham. The complex also houses shrines of Rama-Sita-Lakshmana, Krishna, Hanuman, Ganesha, Durga, Lakshmi and Vishnu. Unique features: the 18 chapters of the Bhagavad Gita are inscribed on the temple walls, and the Krishna temple has paintings of Krishna's life and the Mahabharata by noted painter Raghubir Mulgaonkar. The complex includes a dharamshala (Bhakt Niwas) accommodating around 200 pilgrims.

name: Muktidham Temple
town_description: Nashik, on the banks of the Godavari river in northwestern Maharashtra, is one of India's oldest religious cities - the site of the Nashik Simhastha Kumbh Mela (held every 12 years), the Ramkund bathing ghats, and nearby Trimbakeshwar (one of the 12 Jyotirlingas). It is also known as India's wine capital, with vineyards around the city. Muktidham stands in the Nashik Road suburb, close to the railway station.

travel.airport: Nashik Airport (Ozar), approx. 25-30 km by road (verify); Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj International Airport, Mumbai, approx. 160-170 km.
travel.railway: Nashik Road Railway Station, approx. 1.5-2 km (5-10 minutes by auto-rickshaw).
travel.road: At Nashik Road, approx. 7 km from Nashik city centre; easily reached by city buses, auto-rickshaws and taxis. Parking is available but can be crowded at peak times.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather. Nashik Kumbh Mela years draw very large crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Verify - sources conflict: one lists 6:00 AM-7:00 PM daily, another lists 6:00 AM-12:00 noon and 4:00 PM-8:00 PM daily. Entry is free; modest dress expected; photography is restricted inside the temple.
